title: Fail closed when pipeline reaping cannot establish daemon liveness
description:
## Finding

`thegn dispatch reap --apply` treats any failure to connect to or query the daemon as an empty live-session set. Every spawning/running row is then classified as worker-gone and may be marked `failed` or auto-closed `done` from artifact/report snapshots.

Daemon unreachability is not proof of worker exit. It can be a transient socket/permission/network failure, a wrong endpoint, a daemon stall, or a shutdown window; the existing daemon-lifecycle audit also shows PTY children can outlive daemon teardown. A reap during any of these states can terminally rewrite rows whose workers are still running, free their concurrency slots, and allow duplicate dispatches. The status CAS prevents overwriting a concurrent status edit, but it does not validate worker liveness or an exit generation.

## Evidence at audited commit

* `crates/thegn-host/src/cmd/dispatch.rs:1038-1047` documents daemon-unreachable as every session absent.
* `crates/thegn-host/src/cmd/dispatch.rs:1079-1092` returns `(Vec::new(), false)` for both connect and session-list failures.
* `crates/thegn-host/src/cmd/dispatch.rs:1051-1167` still builds and applies the reap plan when `daemon_up == false`.
* `crates/thegn-core/src/pipeline_reap.rs:117-153` interprets `session_live == false` as worker gone and produces terminal decisions.
* The warning printed by the CLI asserts this is safe, but no positive exit fact is required.

## Implementation constraints

Model unavailable/unknown separately from positively exited. A daemon epoch/restart must not silently equate all old session IDs with completed workers. Reaping may use durable exit stamps/tombstones or an authoritative session-generation record, but ambiguous rows must stay capacity-occupying and require reconciliation. Preserve compare-and-set behavior and do not turn transient unavailability into repeated polling pressure.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Daemon connect/list failure yields an explicit unknown-liveness verdict and `--apply` performs no terminal row transition.
- [ ] A row is auto-reaped only from durable positive exit evidence bound to the correct session/daemon generation.
- [ ] Daemon restart, transient socket failure, timeout, wrong endpoint, and live worker with temporarily unavailable control plane are covered by tests.
- [ ] Ambiguous rows remain slot-occupying and surface an actionable retry/reconcile message.
- [ ] Reap application atomically checks the observed status plus the liveness/exit generation it planned against.
- [ ] The daemon's periodic self-heal and offline CLI share consistent fail-closed semantics.
- [ ] A regression test proves a live worker cannot be marked failed/done or duplicated while the daemon query is unavailable.

## Verification

Run pipeline reap/run/claim tests, daemon restart and transient-unavailability integration tests, two-process claim/reap races, and `just quick`.

## Dependency mapping

* Blocked by THE-171 (LANDED on main) for deterministic session/process shutdown and by THE-208 (NOT landed) for enforced Lead ownership of pipeline judgment.
